messages.author: 2de7c33d05dd213b
messages.subject: Improvement ideas
parts:
Improvement ideas:

1) Allow creating control elements in the output area. Sometimes it's very useful. E.g. I run an app to calculate certain metrics on a long list of data (e.g. stocks performance, websites traffic, ads conversion, costs of projects etc.) and have several tabs: most store tables with aggragated metrics, and one stores some charts specific to each element of the dataset (one stock, one website, one ad or certain project). Ideally I would add a dropdown to the tab output area to filter the charts, but now I need to add it to the input area, which is a bit misleading, as it is relevant to one tab only.

2) Make it possible to save the GUI state (state of all dynamic elements and input values) to a string like php.net/serialize does. Then it would be possible to efficiently use shiny in tasks like data mining, for example, or any other where you look for ideas using a long list of controls. At the moment every time an interesting setup is found I need to either manually save a long list input values to some Excel file or write a script that goes through all the inputs and writes their values to the database. Same for loading the GUI state.

3) Display "Loading..." or similar message after the actionbutton was pressed, but before the output is displayed. Some of my apps take minutes to run and it's not always clear if the button triggered anything at all before all the calculations finished.

4) DataTables are often filled with numbers and therefore it would be extremely useful to be able to filter individual columns using expressions like ">10" or provide 2 fields one under another for numeric and date columns to set the minimum and maximum values.

5) That's the code I used to catch the event of DataTable being changed to color-code the data. I hope that there is an easier way to do it, but I failed to find one. It would be great to have some identification of the mainPanel update. It was fine when you had all the controls in initial DOM in sidebarPanel, but DataTable is created dynamically and I can't that easily add event listeners to it.

$(document).ready(function() {
  // set event handler on #summary mutation
  var MutationObserver = window.MutationObserver || window.WebKitMutationObserver || window.MozMutationObserver;
  var target = document.querySelector('#summary');
  var observer = new MutationObserver(function(mutations) {
      // last mutation during table update is always with DataTables_Table_x_processing target, but there are
      // 2 such events during update, so need an extra check for the previous mutation of DataTables_Table_x_processing
      prevmut = false;
      mutations.forEach(function(mutation) {
          id = /DataTables_Table_(\\d+)_processing/g.exec(mutation.target.id)
          if (id != null) {
            if (mutation.oldValue=='visibility: hidden;' && prevmut) {
              condformat('#DataTables_Table_'+id[1]);
            }
            prevmut = mutation.oldValue=='visibility: visible;';
          }
      });
  });
  // Collect only required mutation data
  observer.observe(target, {
    attributes: true, 
    childList: false, 
    characterData: false,
    subtree: true,
    attributeOldValue: true,
    characterDataOldValue: false
  });
});

parts:
I haven't found an easy way. I write code individually for each app.

I tried to save and replace the input object directly, but obviously it didn't work. Here is the code I tried:

server.R
---------------

library(shiny)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  
  env <- environment()
  
  observe({
    if(input$save>0) {
      isolate({
        assign('SAVED',serialize(input,NULL),env)
      })
    }
  })
  
  observe({
    if(input$load>0) {
      cat('Trying to load input (NROW=',NROW(SAVED),') ')
      unser.SAVED <- unserialize(SAVED)
      cat('Unserialized ')
      cat('input is located in parentenv: ','input' %in% ls(env=parent.env(environment())),' ')
      assign('input',unser.SAVED,parent.env(environment()))
      cat('Loaded ')
    }
  })
  
})

ui.R
------------------

library(shiny)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel("Test quantmod"),
  
  sidebarPanel(
    selectInput("options", "Pick a stock", choices=c('','SPY','IWM','MSFT','GOOG','AAPL','IBM')),
    br(),
    actionButton("save","Save"),
    actionButton("load","Load")
  ),
  
  mainPanel(
  )
))

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Improvement ideas
parts:
Hi Dmitri, thanks so much for the feedback.

#1 is possible already. There's not actually a distinction between input and output "areas" in Shiny, you can put almost any control almost anywhere.

We are working on #2, it's quite easy to do if renderUI is not involved and quite difficult if renderUI is involved!

#3 is coming at some point but in the meantime you could use progressInit/withProgress/setProgress which are available in the shinyIncubator package. You can install it using devtools::install_github("shiny-incubator", "rstudio") and then use ?shinyIncubator::setProgress to get to the docs. I'll tell you up front, the most common mistake with using these functions is forgetting to include progressInit in your UI. It needs to go somewhere (anywhere, as long as it ends up being part of the page; regardless of where you put it, the progress indicator will end up in the upper right corner of your app).

For #5, the latest builds of Shiny on GitHub master branch allows you to provide datatables callbacks as options (the options are passed as an argument to renderDataTables). So something like options=list(fnCreatedRow="function() {...}") should work.

Dmitri,

Until there is an official solution I have an approach to #2 that works. You can try it out if you install the Radiant package at https://github.com/mostly-harmless/radiant or you can go to http://vnijs.rady.ucsd.edu:3838/marketing/ to see it run on shiny-server

In State in the navbar you can save, load, and reset the state of the app. Basically it saves reactiveValues (values in my app) and the input list. When you load a pervious state it is put into a list called state_list. When inputs are initialized they look for a value in state_list first. If that is not available a general starting value is provided. (most) of the code is available in the file linked below.

https://github.com/mostly-harmless/radiant/blob/master/inst/marketing/tools/app/state.R

The 4 functions at the top of the file are used to check if an initial value is available. To see how the functions are used in inputs see, for example, https://github.com/mostly-harmless/radiant/blob/master/inst/marketing/tools/analysis/base.R

messages.subject: Re: Improvement ideas
parts:
For 4), it is now possible in the development version:
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny You can type a string of the form
"lower, upper" to specify a range to filter a column. For example,

runApp(list(
ui = fluidPage(
dataTableOutput('tab1')
),
server = function(input, output) {
output$tab1 = renderDataTable(iris)
}
))

You can type "4,5" (without quotes) in the search box of the first
column so that the rows are filtered using Sepal.Length >=4 &
Sepal.Length <=5.

"lower," means [lower, Inf], and ",upper" means [-Inf, upper].

For 5), I believe it is also possible with the current development
version; see an example at https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/pull/356

Thanks for all the ideas and feedback!

Regards,
Yihui
